plain: Add a feature to an app that already exists.
$comment: Shorter than app because the hard questions were answered once already. If docs/architecture.md is missing, this preset is the wrong one: run rescue, or duet-app for a project that never had documents.
after_last_gate: No more questions about intent. Everything accumulates into the single final round with a recommendation attached.

stages.title: Read the project
stages.plain: Load the existing documents and check they still match the code.
rules: Read CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and docs/ first. That is what they are for.
Spot-check them against the code. A document that has drifted is worse than none, and saying so takes one line.
If they have drifted badly, stop and recommend duet-rescue rather than building on them.
stages.done: A one-line verdict: documents match, or they do not and here is where.
stages.gate_cmd: test -f CLAUDE.md || test -f docs/architecture.md || test -f AGENTS.md

stages.title: Scope
stages.plain: What the feature does, and what it deliberately does not.
stages.ask: What should this do, and is there anything nearby it should deliberately NOT do? Grilling depth follows the setup answer.
stages.done: spec.md holds acceptance criteria and an explicit out-of-scope list.

also_ask.q: I have everything I need. Should I run to the end and bring you the questions at the finish, or stop at each decision?

options.full: Run to the end. Every question waits for the finish.
options.product: Decide the technical things alone. Stop when it changes what someone sees or reads.

also_ask.why: Asked here rather than at setup because this is the moment the person actually knows how much they trust the plan. The setup answer is the default, not the verdict.

stages.title: Research
stages.plain: Codex checks what is current for anything new this touches.
stages.skip_when: The feature uses nothing outside the existing dependency set and touches no external API.
brief_must_ask: What is the current API surface of everything new this feature needs, with signatures rather than summaries?
Does the version in this project's lockfile support the approach, and what is the evidence?
What changed recently enough that a model trained earlier would get it wrong?
stages.done: A briefing where every claim carries a verdict and a source.

stages.title: Plan
stages.plain: Which files change, in what order, and how anyone can tell it worked.
stages.done: A phase list with owners, grounded on the briefing, checked against docs/architecture.md.

stages.title: Build
stages.plain: Claude on the frontend and the words, Codex underneath.

owners.claude: frontend, components, layout, and every word the user reads

rules: Follow the project's existing patterns. A feature that looks imported from another codebase is a defect even when it works.
An architecture change is a decision. It goes in docs/decisions.md or it does not happen.
stages.done: Every acceptance criterion has code behind it.

stages.title: Tests
stages.plain: Codex writes them, at the project's existing level plus the new paths.
stages.done: Suite green, coverage not lower than before, new paths covered.

stages.title: Debate
stages.plain: Both agents review the change and argue about it once.
stages.done: Every concern is fixed, defended with a reason, or in the final question round.

stages.title: Done
stages.plain: Zero outstanding issues, and nothing that worked before is worse.
stages.done: Zero outstanding locally, in tests and deployed, and no regression in existing behaviour.

gate_cmd_note: A stage is done when its gate_cmd exits zero, not when an agent says so. {{cmd.X}} resolves from commands.* in .duet/config.json, detected once by lib/duet-detect.sh. {{out}} is the phase output path. Human gates carry no command, because 'the human confirmed' is not a command.
ask_note: Every gate is a question with two to four options, each naming its consequence, one recommended. Free text stays available and is never the only path. A gate written as a paragraph ending in a question mark is a gate the human has to compose an answer to. See reference/asking.md.
